name: libcoro
listed_description: Open-source experimental library of general-purpose C++20 coroutine primitives, including a task<T> type that the book uses to replace its hand-written task type.
book_benchmark: None. The book only shows the library's coro::task and sync_wait in a short usage example; no timings.
guessed_baseline: hand-written coroutine task types; std::async / std::future
found_in: book: Modern C++ Programming Cookbook, 3rd ed. (2024), ch. 12 C++20 Core Features, section Creating a coroutine task type for asynchronous computations (and Generating a sequence of values with the std::generator type)

name: cppcoro
listed_description: Coroutine library by Lewis Baker used in the book's 2nd edition; the book says it has been unmaintained for years and targets the experimental coroutines TS, so it is only a source of ideas.
book_benchmark: None. The book mentions it only as an unmaintained library and gives no timings.
guessed_baseline: std::async / std::future; hand-written coroutine task types
found_in: book: Modern C++ Programming Cookbook, 3rd ed. (2024), ch. 12 C++20 Core Features, section Creating a coroutine task type for asynchronous computations

name: range-v3
listed_description: Eric Niebler's ranges library on which the C++20 ranges library is based; offers more range adaptors (views) plus mutating actions such as sort, erase and shuffle.
book_benchmark: None. The book says its samples work with both range-v3 and std::ranges; no timings.
guessed_baseline: std::ranges / hand-written loops and std:: algorithms
found_in: book: Modern C++ Programming Cookbook, 3rd ed. (2024), ch. 12 C++20 Core Features, section Iterating over collections with the ranges library
